newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African "animals" could be jailed underground.
newsitem.headline: S.African "animals" could be jailed underground.

text.p: Prisons Minister Sipo Mzimela on Tuesday condemned some of South Africa's criminals as worse than animals and said incarceration in mine shafts was too good for them.
Mzimela told a parliamentary committee the idea of converting disused mines into super-maximum security prisons on the U.S. model was under serious investigation.

"If it is do-able and is cost effective, the fact that it's underground is irrelevant, it's just more secure," he said, noting that more than 100 prisoners escape from South African jails every month.
"So if there is a mine shaft that can be converted into a secure prison and the whole exercise is cost-effective... then of course there's no reason why we shouldn't do that."
Mzimela said the hardened criminals who would be sent down mine shafts were often worse than animals.
"What do you call a father who rapes his three-day-old baby and she dies as a result?

"That person in my definition is worse than an animal. I can give you a whole category of people who fully deserve the categorisation 'worse than animals' and for whom the mine shaft is even too good," the minister said.
He cited a public opinion conducted by the state broadcaster which found that 95 percent of respondents supported the idea of mine shaft jails. "We need to take that into consideration."
Mzimela said that in the U.S. state of Colorado a super-maximum prison had been built into a mountainside.
"So whether you dig into a mountain or dig into the ground it is the same thing.
"We need to emphasise that the conditions under which the most dangerous criminals are held will still be humane and will be consistent with the constitution."
